package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion Platform was compromised during its build process, resulting in official product updates being shipped with a backdoor. This allowed attackers to gain unauthorized access to customer environments, exfiltrate data, and move laterally within networks. The malicious code was inserted upstream, making all distributed binaries during the affected period inherently untrustworthy.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (supply chain injection), runtime (on customer systems)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for certain system characteristics, delays execution to evade detection, then initiates a network connection to a hardcoded command-and-control domain, exfiltrates system information, and awaits further attacker instructions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes covert network communications to an external domain, exfiltrates sensitive system data, and enables remote command execution, all of which are classic backdoor behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate monitoring software should not beacon to unknown external domains or execute remote commands from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may contact vendor servers for updates, but not in a covert, randomized, or command-execution manner.

attack_chain.action: Attacker breaches SolarWinds build environment and injects malicious code into Orion Platform build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is compiled and signed as part of official product updates.

attack_chain.action: Customers download and install contaminated Orion updates, deploying the malicious DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now present and active in customer environments.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code (SUNBURST) executes on customer systems, beacons to attacker-controlled domain, and awaits further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access, can exfiltrate data, and move laterally within the network.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com or similar domains
Randomized execution delays in service processes
Unusual process spawning or command execution by Orion-related services
file_indicators: Presence of files with anomalous timestamps or digital signatures
network_indicators: Subsequent C2 domains as redirected by initial beacon
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns from Orion servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for outbound connections from SolarWinds Orion servers to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Check for the presence and hashes of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll matching known malicious versions. Look for randomized delays and suspicious process activity in Orion service logs. Use EDR/XDR solutions to flag unexpected network or process behaviors from Orion-related binaries.
